first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the concurrent completion and activation declines and has prior evidence across self-serve accounts. Verify its original record and the consequential pricing alternative, since aggressive discounting may win price-sensitive SMBs but could impair sustainable qualified revenue through margin or customer-quality effects.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment to simplify onboarding. Verified evidence shows materially higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and a 3% lift in 30-day retention, directly addressing both declining onboarding completion and activation while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is ruled out for this cycle: despite short-term qualified-revenue lift, its acquired cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Guard the rollout with qualified-revenue and retention cohort checks, since the current activation decline may have causes beyond onboarding friction.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. The competitor's deeper cut and increased price-related churn raise urgency, but the verified pricing evidence shows that a 40% targeted discount produced a cohort with 12% lower 30-day retention and failure to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Simplified onboarding has verified gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention and addresses the current activation and completion declines. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified-revenue cohorts during the test; pricing may require reassessment next cycle with fresh verification capacity.
